buyersGuide.howToChoose: Prioritize sustained sequential write speeds (MB/s) over advertised peak speeds for video editing. Choose drives with robust thermal management to prevent throttling during long transfers. For outdoor or rugged use, select IP65-rated models like the T7 Shield. Avoid drives marketed as 'instant' or 'next-gen' without real-world benchmarks.
pitfalls: Buying based solely on peak read/write speeds (e.g., 20,000 MB/s) which are rarely sustained in practice.
Ignoring thermal throttling during prolonged editing sessions that can reduce performance by 50%+ after 10 minutes.
Assuming all SSDs have the same endurance; high-endurance models like Samsung T7 Shield last longer under heavy use.
marketingToIgnore: ‘Revolutionary’ or ‘next-gen’ claims without hands-on testing — these are marketing labels, not performance indicators.
Ignoring IP ratings when using SSDs in dusty environments; IP65 is the minimum for outdoor work.
Treating 20,000 MB/s as a real-world benchmark; consumer drives rarely exceed 1,000 MB/s sustained.

runs.query: best email marketing service for a small newsletter

output.summary: For a small newsletter, MailerLite and Brevo (formerly Sendinblue) are strong options, but MailerLite's free tier is limited by strict onboarding approvals. Brevo offers generous limits and better deliverability but lacks a free tier. Kit (ConvertKit) excels for creators with automations but isn't ideal if you need the absolute cheapest option.

buyersGuide.howToChoose: When selecting an email service for a small newsletter, prioritize deliverability and ease of use over price. Focus on how well it handles inbox placement (Gmail/Outlook) and whether its free tier is truly usable without approval hurdles. For creators, automation features matter more than raw send limits.
pitfalls: Choosing a service solely because it has the lowest monthly cost ignores hidden costs like upgrade fees or lost subscribers from poor deliverability.
Ignoring onboarding requirements can delay your first campaign launch, wasting time and momentum.
Assuming all services have equal spam filters overlooks that some platforms (like Brevo) are known for higher bounce rates with new accounts.
marketingToIgnore: ‘Revolutionary AI’ claims in listicles don’t translate to real-world deliverability improvements for small lists.
Free-tier limitations framed as ‘premium features’ when they’re actually dealbreakers for beginners.
Higher send limits marketed as ‘unlimited’ without clear caps or throttling that affect performance.
